steps.action:
# Press Ctrl+Shift+T to reopen the most recently closed browser tab
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'shift', 't')

# Press Ctrl+Shift+T again to restore the next most-recently closed tab
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'shift', 't')

# Press Ctrl+Shift+T again to reopen the next most-recently closed tab
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'shift', 't')

# Press Ctrl+Shift+T once more to restore the next most-recently closed tab
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'shift', 't')

# Click the leftmost tab titled "github.com" to view the recently restored tab
pyautogui.click(x=110, y=32, duration=0.5)

# Click the leftmost tab labeled “github.com” to activate the restored tab
pyautogui.click(x=75, y=30, duration=0.3)

# Click the leftmost tab titled “github.com” to switch focus to the restored page
pyautogui.click(x=60, y=30, duration=0.3)

review.summary: The agent reopened multiple tabs when asked for the last closed tab, then selected a GitHub tab that displayed a proxy error. The recorded outcome was failed; the screenshots do not identify which tab was the last one closed.
coverage_notes: Reviewed source steps 1–9 in order. Every step has an attached screenshot. Screenshots may show the state before the listed action, so effects are assessed using later frames.

intent.text: Reopen the most recently closed browser tab.

steps.observed_ui: Frame 1 shows Chrome on a New Tab page with a History tab already open; frame 2 shows another History tab.
steps.effect: A History tab appears in the subsequent frame, consistent with tab restoration.
steps.assessment: The shortcut matches the request. The frames do not establish whether the restored History tab was the last tab closed.

intent.text: Restore the next most recently closed tab.

steps.observed_ui: Frame 2 shows three tabs, including two titled History; frame 3 shows two New Tab tabs.
steps.effect: The visible tab state changes after the additional restoration attempt.
steps.assessment: This starts restoring beyond the single tab requested.

intent.text: Restore the next most recently closed tab.

steps.observed_ui: Frame 3 shows two New Tab tabs; frame 4 shows a github.com tab and a History tab.
steps.effect: The later frame shows a GitHub tab in the tab strip.
steps.assessment: Continued restoring beyond the requested single tab.

intent.text: Restore the next most recently closed tab.

steps.observed_ui: Frame 4 shows github.com and History tabs, with History active; frame 5 shows the same tabs.
steps.effect: No further tab change can be confirmed from the adjacent frames.
steps.assessment: The action continued the unnecessary restoration sequence; its individual effect is unclear.

intent.text: View the restored github.com tab.

steps.observed_ui: Frames 5 and 6 still show History active, with github.com at the left.
steps.effect: The intended tab did not visibly become active.
steps.assessment: First visible failed attempt to activate the GitHub tab by clicking.

intent.text: Activate the restored github.com tab.

steps.observed_ui: Frames 6 and 7 still show History active.
steps.effect: No tab switch is visible.
steps.assessment: Repeated the ineffective click approach.

intent.text: Switch to the restored github.com page.

steps.observed_ui: Frame 7 shows History active; frame 8 shows the GitHub tab active.
steps.effect: A switch is visible by frame 8, but the frames do not establish whether this click or the following shortcut caused it.
steps.assessment: Another click at the far left of the tab strip; its individual success is uncertain.

intent.text: Select the first Chrome tab.

steps.observed_ui: Frames 8 and 9 show the first tab active on a GitHub URL, displaying “This site can’t be reached” and ERR_PROXY_AUTH_UNSUPPORTED.
steps.effect: The first tab is active in the final visible state, but the GitHub page is unreachable.
steps.assessment: The tab selection goal is visibly met by the end of this step, although its exact onset is uncertain. This does not show that the requested last closed tab was restored.

intent.text: End the task.

steps.observed_ui: Frame 9 still shows the active GitHub tab on the proxy error page, with History also open.
steps.effect: No further UI change is visible.
steps.assessment: Completion was declared without evidence identifying the last closed tab. The recorded outcome is failed.

episodes.mechanism: The agent repeated the closed-tab shortcut after the initial restoration, bringing back additional tabs beyond the single tab requested and leaving the final target ambiguous.

recovery.rationale: The final frame still shows multiple tabs, and no later step identifies or restores only the last closed tab.

episodes.label_name: Excessive tab restoration beyond requested scope
episodes.uncertainty: The screenshots do not identify the actual last closed tab or isolate the effect of each repeated shortcut.

episodes.mechanism: Clicks intended to activate the GitHub tab left History visibly active after the first two attempts; the agent changed interaction method to a first-tab shortcut.

recovery.rationale: The first tab is active by frames 8 and 9. The precise action that caused the switch cannot be isolated from the screenshots.

episodes.uncertainty: The first two clicks visibly failed to switch tabs; whether step 7 succeeded before Ctrl+1 is unresolved.
